request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (30,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 32.2% (95% band 31.9% to 48.8%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; 1: +0.6; >= 2: +2.4 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.54, 95% band [+2.42, +2.71]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 20.6% (95% band 19.7% to 26.5%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 79999: +0.55; 80000-159999: +0.08; 160000-449999: -0.38; 450000-659999: -1; 660000-689999: +1; >= 690000: -2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.34, 95% band [-1.40, -0.97]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 9.4% (95% band 6.6% to 11.4%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 1290: +0.176; 1291-77899: -0.1; >= 77900: -1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.59, 95% band [-0.69, -0.30]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 5.4% (95% band 1.8% to 7.9%); rank 3 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.37 (95% band [+0.10, +0.70]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 201,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 5.0% (95% band 0.6% to 5.3%); rank 4 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 156258: 0; >= 156259: +0.5 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.60, 95% band [+0.04, +0.61]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 4.9% (95% band 1.5% to 6.7%); rank 4 to 7 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 11252: -0.004; >= 11253: -0.1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.11, 95% band [-0.24, +0.01]).
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 3.0% (95% band 0.0% to 4.1%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.00, 95% band [-0.11, +0.15]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.0% to 2.5%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.06, 95% band [-0.12, +0.13]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 0.4% (95% band 0.0% to 1.8%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.02, 95% band [-0.01, +0.09]).

Interactions: the model has 35 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & LIMIT_BAL`: share of importance 1.8% (95% band 1.4% to 3.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.33 (95% band +2.19 to +2.64) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +2.65 (95% band +2.30 to +2.96) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.35 (95% band -1.43 to -0.97) when `PAY_0` = -2, -1.03 (95% band -1.36 to -0.64) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 1.6% (95% band 0.0% to 1.1%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.64 (95% band -0.79 to -0.30) when `AGE` = 23, -0.48 (95% band -0.74 to -0.27) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: -0.13 (95% band -0.22 to +0.13) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.04 (95% band -0.15 to +0.18) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 1.5% (95% band 0.0% to 1.2%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.63 (95% band +0.10 to +0.86) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.17 (95% band +0.10 to +0.68) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: +0.08 (95% band -0.25 to +0.05) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.39 (95% band -0.42 to -0.02) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.

  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.77 (95% band -0.91 to -0.35) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.41 (95% band -0.54 to -0.12) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.1% to 1.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.66 (95% band -0.87 to -0.25) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.63 (95% band -0.85 to -0.29) when `BILL_AMT2` = 195,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 195,000: +0.60 (95% band +0.04 to +0.64) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.63 (95% band -0.01 to +0.70) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
- `PAY_0 & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.5% to 2.3%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.30 (95% band +2.09 to +2.50) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +2.48 (95% band +2.24 to +2.78) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.34 (95% band +0.01 to +0.69) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.52 (95% band +0.21 to +1.00) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.2% to 1.9%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.49 (95% band -1.67 to -1.04) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -1.24 (95% band -1.43 to -0.93) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.27 (95% band -0.44 to -0.03) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.02 (95% band -0.21 to +0.25) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_AMT2 & AGE`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 0.9%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.04 (95% band -0.28 to +0.05) when `AGE` = 23, -0.14 (95% band -0.23 to +0.06) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.00 (95% band -0.13 to +0.13) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -0.09 (95% band -0.21 to +0.16) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
- `BILL_AMT2 & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.1%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 195,000: +0.89 (95% band +0.04 to +0.73) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, +0.38 (95% band +0.02 to +0.54) when `PAY_AMT3` = 17,600.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 17,600: +0.23 (95% band -0.09 to +0.20) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.27 (95% band -0.28 to +0.08) when `BILL_AMT2` = 195,000.
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.47 (95% band +0.10 to +0.74) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.40 (95% band +0.10 to +0.81) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.66 (95% band -0.82 to -0.32) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.73 (95% band -0.86 to -0.28) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.1% to 1.7%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.60 (95% band +2.46 to +2.80) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +2.45 (95% band +2.32 to +2.66) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by repayment status in September 2005, the latest month, which accounts for about a third of the model's importance: applicants who were already at least two months behind on payments carry a much higher predicted risk (about +2.4 on the log-odds scale) than those who paid in full, while one month of delay adds a smaller increase."},{"id":2,"text":"The size of the given credit (LIMIT_BAL) is the second most important driver, at about a fifth of importance: smaller credit limits tend to raise predicted risk, while very large limits (690,000 NT dollars and above) are associated with lower risk, though this pattern is uneven across the range."},{"id":3,"text":"The amount paid in September 2005 (PAY_AMT1) matters moderately: payments up to about 1,290 NT dollars are linked to slightly higher risk, and payments of 77,900 NT dollars or more are linked to lower risk."},{"id":4,"text":"The bill amounts for September and August 2005 (BILL_AMT1 and BILL_AMT2) add smaller, less certain increases in predicted risk as bills grow, and the data do not settle the shape of the BILL_AMT1 effect between its low and high values."},{"id":5,"text":"Age, education, and the earlier payment amounts (PAY_AMT2 and PAY_AMT3) contribute little or nothing resolvable: their effects are small and their uncertainty ranges include no effect."},{"id":6,"text":"Several interactions matter: the effect of repayment status is somewhat stronger for applicants with larger credit limits, and the penalty for a small credit limit is weaker when recent payments are large, so the drivers should not be read in isolation."},{"id":7,"text":"Most of the model's signal therefore comes from recent repayment behaviour and credit limit, with the remaining features playing a minor and partly uncertain role."}]}
